Chapter 8: The Practice of Silence and Sabbath
As the year started winding down, our experimenter found herself entering a season of quiet. You know, the Bible’s teachings about silence—especially when it comes to women—can stir up a lot of questions. Is silence just a way to keep people quiet, or could it actually be a path to deeper listening?
To get to the heart of it, she began setting aside special time each week for intentional silence. I’m talking no phone, no TV, no endless to-do lists—just space to actually be still. At first, the quiet felt a little uncomfortable, maybe even unsettling. Her mind buzzed with worries and all those half-finished tasks. But as the minutes ticked by, something shifted. The noise slowly faded, and suddenly, there was this new sense of clarity.
In that stillness, she started noticing things she’d always missed—the whisper of the wind, the steady rhythm of her own breath, and the gentle sense that God was right there. That’s when it clicked: silence isn’t about erasing your own voice. It’s about making space for what really matters.
Alongside silence, she tried something else: Sabbath. Setting aside one day each week just for rest. In a world that’s always hurrying and pushing for more, the very idea of stopping can feel almost rebellious, can’t it? But as she learned to put down her work and actually rest, she discovered a new kind of freedom. The world didn’t fall apart just because she paused. In fact, everything seemed a little brighter, a little more possible.
Most of us don’t realize just how much we need real rest until we finally give ourselves permission to stop. For her, Sabbath became more than just a rule or tradition—it turned into a gift. A gentle reminder that we are so much more than what we accomplish.
By the time this chapter drew to a close, she’d realized something important. Silence and rest aren’t signs of weakness at all—they’re actually sources of real strength. They open up space for reflection, for gratitude, and for the quiet, powerful work happening deep inside our souls.
